title: “The Lord possessed me in the beginning of his way” — what is the wisdom that speaks in Proverbs 8?
summary: Proverbs 8:1 and 8:12 say that the speaker is wisdom, and 8:22–30 have her say she was with the Lord before the earth and “by him” when he made it. The verses quoted do not say what kind of thing the speaker is.
text: KJV Proverbs 8:1: “Doth not wisdom cry? and understanding put forth her voice?” KJV Proverbs 8:12: “I wisdom dwell with prudence, and find out knowledge of witty inventions.” KJV Proverbs 8:22–23: “The Lord possessed me in the beginning of his way, before his works of old.” “I was set up from everlasting, from the beginning, or ever the earth was.” KJV Proverbs 8:29–30: “When he gave to the sea his decree, that the waters should not pass his commandment: when he appointed the foundations of the earth:” “Then I was by him, as one brought up with him: and I was daily his delight, rejoicing always before him;” KJV Proverbs 9:1: “Wisdom hath builded her house, she hath hewn out her seven pillars:”
reasoning: The speaker is named as “wisdom” in 8:1 and 8:12. In 8:22–31 she says that the Lord possessed her “in the beginning of his way”, that she was “set up from everlasting”, that she was “by him” when he laid the foundations of the earth, and that she was his delight. In 9:1 “Wisdom hath builded her house”. The verses quoted do not say whether the speaker is a figure of speech for a quality of the Lord, a quality of the creation, a being distinct from the Lord, or a personification used only to teach. Possible readings: (1) a poetic personification of the Lord’s wisdom, as the book personifies wisdom elsewhere; (2) a personification of the order the Lord put into the creation; (3) a being that the passage speaks of as distinct from the Lord. The record does not decide between them.
scope: Q marks a question the passage leaves open. It is not a finding of contradiction or of scientific error. The question is limited to the verses quoted. The record does not examine other passages that speak of wisdom, does not say that any reading is the right one, and does not rest on the Greek verb of 8:22, which is the subject of its own T record. The Hebrew and the Greek were not quoted for this question.

sides.label: A
sides.quote: The Lord possessed me in the beginning of his way

title: “The words of Agur the son of Jakeh” — who are Agur, Jakeh, Ithiel and Ucal?
summary: Proverbs 30:1 names Agur the son of Jakeh as the speaker and Ithiel and Ucal as those addressed. The verses quoted do not say who any of the four were, or where or when they lived.
text: KJV Proverbs 30:1–3: “The words of Agur the son of Jakeh, even the prophecy: the man spake unto Ithiel, even unto Ithiel and Ucal,” “Surely I am more brutish than any man, and have not the understanding of a man.” “I neither learned wisdom, nor have the knowledge of the holy.” KJV Nehemiah 11:7: “And these are the sons of Benjamin; Sallu the son of Meshullam, the son of Joed, the son of Pedaiah, the son of Kolaiah, the son of Maaseiah, the son of Ithiel, the son of Jesaiah.” A search of the packaged KJV for the words “Agur”, “Jakeh” and “Ucal” finds Proverbs 30:1 only; for “Ithiel” it finds Proverbs 30:1 and Nehemiah 11:7.
reasoning: The verse gives four names and calls the speech “the prophecy”. It does not say who Agur was, who Jakeh was, whether Ithiel and Ucal were people, pupils or something else, or what the relation of the speaker to them was. The verses that follow (30:2–3) are the speaker’s own account of himself and do not name or describe the others. The one other occurrence of “Ithiel” in the KJV, Nehemiah 11:7, is a name in the line of Sallu, one of the sons of Benjamin (“the son of Ithiel, the son of Jesaiah”); the record quotes it as context and does not say it is the Ithiel of Proverbs. Possible readings: persons otherwise unknown who are named only here; names that stand for a role the verse does not define; or names that a reader of the first audience would have known. The record does not decide between them.
scope: Q marks a question the passage leaves open. It is not a finding of contradiction or of scientific error. The question is limited to the verses quoted; the word search covers the packaged KJV text only and is a word search. The record does not say that any reading is the right one, and does not rest on the Hebrew or the Greek of the verse, whose wording is the subject of its own T record.

title: “What is his name, and what is his son’s name, if thou canst tell?” — who is the one asked after in Proverbs 30:4?
summary: Proverbs 30:4 asks who ascended into heaven and descended, who gathered the wind, bound the waters and established the ends of the earth, and ends “what is his name, and what is his son’s name, if thou canst tell?”. The verses quoted ask the question and do not name an answer.
text: KJV Proverbs 30:2–4: “Surely I am more brutish than any man, and have not the understanding of a man.” “I neither learned wisdom, nor have the knowledge of the holy.” “Who hath ascended up into heaven, or descended? who hath gathered the wind in his fists? who hath bound the waters in a garment? who hath established all the ends of the earth? what is his name, and what is his son's name, if thou canst tell?” KJV Proverbs 30:5–6: “Every word of God is pure: he is a shield unto them that put their trust in him.” “Add thou not unto his words, lest he reprove thee, and thou be found a liar.”
reasoning: Verse 4 is a run of questions that ends by asking for a name and a son’s name. The verses before it are the speaker’s statement about himself, and the verses after it speak of “every word of God” and of not adding to “his words”. None of the verses quoted names the one asked after, or says whether the question expects an answer, expects no answer, or is meant to show that no human can answer it. Possible readings: a rhetorical question whose answer is the Lord, with “his son’s name” left unexplained; a question that expects no answer to show that the matter is beyond the speaker; or a question put to a hearer who is expected to supply a name. The record does not decide between them.
